subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic group-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, and memory boundaries become the public contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior crosses channel routing, durable agent creation, memory isolation, per-agent skills/config, resource lifecycle, and security boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Design a generic identity-to-agent contract first
options.body: Create an opt-in, admin-authorized lifecycle and memory contract that Feishu can implement without Feishu-only hidden policy.

options.title: Keep session-only routing plus explicit subagents
options.body: Continue using group_sender or group_topic_sender session scoping, static bindings, and explicit thread-bound sessions_spawn until a broader contract is approved.

options.title: Defer to deployment-specific plugins
options.body: Leave automatic provisioning to external deployments or plugins unless a missing OpenClaw channel/API seam is identified.

recommendation.title: Design a generic identity-to-agent contract first
recommendation.body: Create an opt-in, admin-authorized lifecycle and memory contract that Feishu can implement without Feishu-only hidden policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue starts with Feishu channel ownership before any shared core seam is added, and package metadata identifies m1heng as the Feishu plugin contact.
